page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-288-lssd-metal is a bare-metal server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 144 physical cores and 288 dedicated vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 1080.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, providing 3.75 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the server includes six NVMe SSDs totaling 16,242 GB of capacity. No GPUs are present on this instance.

In benchmark testing, this server demonstrates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, ranking in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU tests. The DDR5 memory subsystem achieves top-tier read and write bandwidth, with uncached read speeds of 1086.87 GB/sec and write speeds of 428.24 GB/sec. The processor's advanced instruction support, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), contributes to top-tier performance in cryptographic operations, database transactions, and prompt processing for medium-sized LLM inference. However, single-core performance is moderate, placing in the middle 50% for stress-ng single-core tests, and text generation for small LLM models is relatively weak.

Given its massive core count, high-speed DDR5 memory, and extensive local NVMe SSD storage, this bare-metal server offers high resource density for workloads requiring massive parallel processing and low-latency storage access. It is highly suited for large-scale database operations, high-throughput static web serving, multi-threaded data decompression, and compute-heavy enterprise applications. The lack of GPU acceleration makes it less suitable for heavy deep learning training, but its AMX capabilities allow it to handle CPU-based AI inference tasks efficiently.
